exact_excerpts: Juniper Reach Library should extend its room-booking pilot for six weeks to test access and reliability before considering more rooms.
The first eight weeks show demand, without establishing reliable access.
Two rooms offered free, two-hour bookings during staffed hours
118 of 160 slots were reserved, and 91 were used.
Of 42 voluntary feedback respondents, 25 valued predictable space for study or small-group work; 17 struggled to find a slot or complete a booking.
Of 42 voluntary feedback respondents
These responses cannot establish how widespread those difficulties are.
Eighteen of 27 unused reservations belonged to four repeat bookers. Most slots never reserved fell before noon on weekdays.

Cancellation habits may contribute to unused reservations, while residents’ availability may explain low weekday-morning demand; neither explanation is established. Unused reservations alone do not measure unmet demand
adding rooms would not necessarily address either problem.
Juniper Reach Library should extend its room-booking pilot for six weeks to test access and reliability before considering more rooms.
The online form requires an email address, while telephone bookings depend on the front-desk supervisor’s availability.
Three of the 17 respondents reporting difficulties said the email requirement or limited telephone coverage prevented a booking.
During the extension, any trained desk worker should accept telephone and in-person reservations, with every route using the same inventory.
Reminders and simple cancellation could help release unwanted reservations, though effectiveness remains unmeasured.
Timely cancellation counts toward the 85% threshold, but releasing a slot does not establish that someone uses it.
The service manager should arrange training and publish weekly reservation, attendance, cancellation and unaccommodated-request totals by booking route and time of day.
Desk workers should record requests consistently, including when rooms are full.
Juniper Reach Library should extend its room-booking pilot for six weeks to test access and reliability before considering more rooms.
After the six-week extension, all three proposed conditions must be met before considering expansion

After the six-week extension, all three proposed conditions must be met before considering expansion: trained staff can cover every staffed opening period; at least 85% of reservations during the extension are used or cancelled before their start; and unaccommodated requests persist despite the changes in at least four of the six weeks.
Timely cancellation counts toward the 85% threshold, but releasing a slot does not establish that someone uses it.
Meeting these conditions would support considering expansion, without establishing how many rooms are needed.
If coverage or reliability remains weak, revise the process and reassess before expanding.
